notes.text:
**Stronger than filed: this is the normal outcome, not two stale leftovers.**

`hkb gc --yes` at teardown tonight removed **nothing** and skipped three worktrees, every one held by a recycled process:

```
skip .claude/worktrees/kb-191-1: still locked by a live session (pid 195775)
skip .claude/worktrees/kb-217-1: still locked by a live session (pid 463367)
skip .claude/worktrees/kb-223-1: still locked by a live session (pid 7992)
gc: 0 worktree(s) removed, 0 branch(es) deleted, ...
```

All three are `claude bg-spare --bg-spare /tmp/cc-daemon-1000/.../spare/<id>.claim.sock`. The third, `kb-223-1`, is track #223's own root worktree — stranded within minutes of the track finishing and merging, on this same session.

So the leak is not occasional. **Every completed worker strands its worktree**, because the harness recycles the process rather than exiting it, and `pidAlive` is therefore always true. `hkb gc` currently cannot reclaim anything on this machine at all — its removal count has been zero for every card that finished tonight.

That also means the branch sweep never runs for those cards (a worktree holds the branch), so `kb/*` branches accumulate alongside the checkouts.

The fix in the Done when is unchanged; only the priority argument is stronger — this is not cleanup hygiene, it is `hkb gc` being inert for its main job on any host whose harness pools processes.
